title: Part (b): constant-probability failure in the incoherent flat regime is unproven

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**[proof-gap | SCOPE/UNIFORMITY]** `thm:fail`, `lem:colvar`, `lem:froblb`, `rem:cure`.

The single-column Paley-Zygmund failure constant is $c=\tfrac9{16}(1+\rho^\star/q)^{-1}$. For an incoherent flat heaviest column ($\rho^\star\asymp 1/m$, $q=s/(mn)$) this gives $c\asymp s/n\to0$: the single-column device yields **no constant-probability failure** there. The proof concedes this and defers to the Frobenius certificate.

The abstract claims a 'coherence-free relative-error barrier... for every matrix.' To honor that, `lem:froblb` must be shown to deliver constant-probability Frobenius lower deviation $\|A-A_k^{\mathrm{rand}}\|_F>(1+\varepsilon)\tau_k$ **uniformly including the incoherent flat case**, under the side condition $s\ge 16\,mn\,\rho_\bullet$ (`eq:failcond`). Required: (i) prove the side condition is automatic/harmless in the incoherent flat regime; (ii) unify the single-column and Frobenius arguments so the two together provably cover all coherence regimes (incoherent through maximally coherent, where it inflates to $s\asymp mn$ via `prop:spike`/`prop:coupon`).
